Sampled HR@10 with one positive and 99 negatives measures ranking within 100 candidates. It does not establish full-catalog top-10 quality: Krichene and Rendle show that sampling can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Keep the pinned benchmark unchanged, but interpret improvements as evidence for that benchmark; the simulator’s full-catalog recommendations address a different ranking task. [On Sampled Metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For this design, use a paired, category-stratified user bootstrap: retain each user’s two models’ hit indicators on identical candidates; resample 200 users with replacement independently within each category; compute each category’s mean hit difference, then average the four differences. Use, for example, 10,000 replicates for a 95% interval. Pairing preserves covariance between models. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidate samples; they exclude training-seed and candidate-resampling variability. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points, so modest gains can represent few users. [Paired bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-1.14.0/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)

Repeatedly selecting checkpoints and hyperparameters on the same validation users creates selection optimism; an ordinary bootstrap interval for the selected winner does not correct that adaptive search. Cawley and Talbot show that selection overfitting can rival reported algorithm differences. Under the limited budget, a practical implication is to predefine checkpoint-selection rules, cache per-user outcomes, examine paired differences and category consistency, and treat small isolated peaks cautiously. An interval crossing zero indicates unresolved improvement, not equivalence; even an interval above zero remains exploratory after extensive selection. Reserve held-out evaluation for the final chosen model. [Selection-bias study](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
